tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberField.summary: Layers 0-2 are essentially already built, in TauCeti, under exactly the file tree and the names this roadmap prescribes (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/Places, Approximation, RayClass): the Place carrier and normalized absolute values with the product formula, Artin-Whaples weak approximation in the mixed-completion form with the total sign homomorphism, and the whole modulus/ray-class package - Modulus with its gcd-lcm lattice, IsCongrOne, congruenceSubgroup, RayClassGroup, idealClass as a monoid homomorphism on the coprime submonoid with both triviality criteria, classMap, finiteUnitsMap, the ray-class exact sequence with the unit-sign obstruction, finiteness, the class-number formula, and the narrow class group. All of it is sorry-free. Mathlib supplies the substrate: both place types, the isometric identification of an infinite completion with R or C, the canonical embedding and its ideal lattice with covolume, the Dedekind zeta residue, the cyclotomic Galois group, class-group finiteness and Dirichlet's unit theorem. From Layer 3 onward the libraries have carriers but no theory. Genuinely missing: every power-saving error term (Mathlib's ZLattice counting gives limits only, and IsLipschitzParametrizable does not exist), all ray-class ideal counting, the entire adelic development beyond bare definitions - Mathlib's AdeleRing.lean is 135 lines of carriers, with no local compactness, no compactness of the additive quotient, no strong approximation, no idele norm and no norm-one subgroup - the idelic ray-class dictionary, adele base change, Hecke and ray class characters, all three infinity types, and orders with their Picard groups. Layer 5's discreteness of K in the full adele ring is the one piece of adelic content already proved (in TauCeti).

targets.target: one type indexing all places of K, with a uniform API for ranging over them
targets.note: `Place K := HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) ⊕ InfinitePlace K` is exactly the uniform indexing type the layer asks for, sitting on Mathlib's two place types.

targets.target: comparison of `v.adicCompletion K` with its nonarchimedean local-field data
targets.note: TauCeti proves `IsNonarchimedeanLocalField (v.adicCompletion K)` for a finite place, with the residue field identified as the quotient of the ring of integers by v and its cardinality as `Ideal.absNorm`; Mathlib's class then supplies the DVR, finite residue field and compact integers. This is Number Field Arithmetic Layer 5.1, the comparison this layer says to consume.

targets.target: `w.Completion` topologically isomorphic to ℝ for real w and ℂ for complex w, compatibly with the embedding of K
targets.note: Mathlib gives both ring equivalences and isometry equivalences, so the identification is topological, and `extensionEmbedding_coe` supplies the compatibility with the embedding of K.

targets.target: the normalized local absolute value on each side of the partition
targets.note: `normalizedAbsValue : Place K → K →*₀ ℝ`; the completion-side absolute value is defined separately and proved to agree on the image of K.

targets.target: agreement with `HeightOneSpectrum.valuation` at finite places
targets.note: The finite component is defined through the adic absolute value, and the explicit `N𝔭 ^ (−v x)` formula is proved for algebraic integers.

targets.target: the real and squared-complex formulas at infinite places
targets.note: The squaring at complex places is Mathlib's `mult`; both cases are separate lemmas in TauCeti.

targets.target: finiteness of the set of places where `|x|_v ≠ 1` for `x ∈ Kˣ`
targets.note: Stated with hypothesis `x ≠ 0` in K rather than for `Kˣ`; same content.

targets.target: the global product formula, as a transport of `NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one`
targets.note: The TauCeti theorem is literally the transport onto the `Place K` carrier that the layer prescribes, with `finprod_normalizedAbsValue_inl` as the finite half.

targets.target: functoriality of the local absolute values under a finite extension, with local degrees in the exponents
targets.note: The ingredients are all present (comap of infinite places, `mult`/local degrees, the completion algebra map and its tower compatibility), but there is no theorem relating `normalizedAbsValue` over L at w to `normalizedAbsValue` over K at w|K with the local degree as exponent; nothing in `Global/Places/` mentions a finite extension.

States the product formula and the places of the rational function field: the function-field analogue of this layer, parallel rather than shared.

targets.target: Artin–Whaples weak approximation in the mixed-completion form `weakApproximation_denseRange`
targets.note: Proved with the exact prescribed name, and in the genuine completions `v.adicCompletion K` and `w.Completion` rather than in copies of K carrying the place topologies.

targets.target: simultaneous independent finite-place targets and real-place signs for one element of `Kˣ`
targets.note: Both conclusions are `∃ x : Kˣ`, exactly the formulation the layer insists on so that `0` cannot satisfy a negative sign request; the second even prescribes the valuations exactly, which is the form needed to move an ideal.

targets.target: the total sign homomorphism to the product of `ℤˣ` over real places, and its surjectivity on `Kˣ`
targets.note: `signHom : Kˣ →* ({w // w.IsReal} → ℤˣ)` is `fieldUnitSignature` read through `Units.signEquiv ℝ`; surjectivity is inherited from `fieldUnitSignature_surjective`, itself a weak-approximation statement.

targets.target: recording that the restriction of the sign map to `(𝓞 K)ˣ` need not be surjective (the narrow-class obstruction)
targets.note: The layer asks only that the failure be *recorded*. It is: the `signHom` module docstring states it in those words, and the Layer 2 exact sequence measures it (the image of the unit residue-sign map is the kernel of the map to the ray class group). No theorem asserts nonsurjectivity at a named field, though the witness is available in the library — `Multiquadratic.twoRank_eq_zero_of_minpoly_eq_X_sq_sub_three` with `narrowTwoRank_eq_ncard_ramifiedPrimes_sub_one` gives Cl⁺ ≠ Cl for ℚ(√3).

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamifi.summary: The libraries have the foundational half of this roadmap and essentially none of the ramification theory. Mathlib supplies IsNonarchimedeanLocalField with its consequences (discrete valuation ring of integers, finite residue field, compact integers, value group isomorphic to Z^m0), the instance for Q_p, the spectral norm and Krasner's lemma, Eisenstein polynomials, differentIdeal with its unramified criterion and tower transitivity, a general arithmetic Frobenius IsArithFrobAt for invariant extensions, the inertia subgroup of a valuation subring, and finite fields. TauCeti adds, sorry-free, the normalized valuation and absolute value with a full API, the unit filtration with both membership forms and all its point-set properties, both graded pieces separately, the Teichmuller lift with its uniqueness characterisation and mu_{q-1} = k^x, Henselianity of the integer ring, openness and closedness of the power subgroup in the prime-to-residue-characteristic regime, and the separable-closure comparison that Layer 4 asks for as its ambient model. What is genuinely missing is large and coherent: the whole finite-extension package of Layer 0 (no finiteExtensionNormedField, no finiteExtensionValuativeRel, no uniqueness of the extended valuation, no intrinsic e and f, no natCastValuation, no absoluteRamificationIndex), the structure of K^x as Z x O^x and O^x as mu x U(1), the local logarithm on deep units and every consequence of it (the power-class counts, the mixed-characteristic openness regime, the deep-units-are-squares threshold and its sharpness), all of Layer 2 (the local unramified predicate, the residue correspondence, frobeniusAlgEquiv, K_f, K^ur, the norm group and the norm-equation criterion), and all of Layers 3 and 4. In particular Mathlib defines no higher ramification group in either numbering - RingTheory/Valuation/RamificationGroup.lean stops at the inertia subgroup - and there is no Herbrand function, no Hasse-Arf, no tame/wild predicate, no local monogenicity, no tame character and no Iwasawa presentation. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic.summary: This roadmap is built, end to end, in Tau Ceti, and its own summary is out of date: it says multiquadratic extensions and genus theory are "entirely absent upstream", which is true of Mathlib but not of TauCeti, where TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/ carries about a hundred files covering all four layers, sorry-free. Layer 0's square-class descent, the 2^n degree theorem, the abelian exponent-2 Galois group with the explicit sign-pattern isomorphism Gal ≅ (Z/2)^n, and the intermediate-field/F_2-subspace correspondence are all present, generalised beyond the stated case to an arbitrary base field and index type. Layer 1's splitting law and the Legendre-vector Frobenius are proved, as are the prime-discriminant and fundamental-discriminant packages the layer warns about, and exists_transversal_family has been migrated. Layer 2's elementary-two quotient (kept explicitly distinct from the 2-torsion subgroup, with the equal-cardinality theorem), units_sq_index_le and the ambiguous class number formula are all there. Layer 3's summit is reached: the genus field is characterised by a universal property, the prime-discriminant compositum is proved to have it in both signatures, the narrow class group and narrow genus field exist (the layer says "Mathlib has neither", which remains true of Mathlib only), Gal(K_gen/K) is identified with the elementary-two quotient of the narrow class group compatibly with the ideal-theoretic Artin map, and the 2-rank formula 2-rank Cl+(K) = t-1 is proved for either signature, with the ordinary rank pinned to t-1 or t-2 and the roadmap's own counterexample Q(sqrt 3) recorded as a theorem. Nothing in this roadmap is genuinely missing.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithm.summary: Most of this roadmap is already built, in Tau Ceti, and its summary ("nothing instantiates the Frobenius API for number fields; Mathlib/RingTheory/Frobenius.lean has no reverse dependencies") is out of date: TauCeti now instantiates it in full. Layer 2 is essentially complete - relative Frobenius existence, uniqueness and Subsingleton at unramified primes, artinSymbol with its whole comparison API, the restriction theorem IsArithFrobAt.restrictNormal, the tower formula exists_isArithFrobAt_pow_inertiaDeg, and the ideal-theoretic artinHomAway with all five named contract declarations spelled exactly as the roadmap freezes them - with only the place-dependent complexConjugationAt of 2.7 missing (Mathlib has the CM specialisation). Layer 4 is built outright: relDiscr is a named definition at Dedekind generality, with non-vanishing, the reconciliation with NumberField.discr, the tower formula, the IsUnramifiedAt ramification criterion, ramifiedSupport with both membership characterisations, discr_smulTower and Stickelberger's congruence. Layer 1 has 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4 (the double-coset bijection with its value formula, naturality and invariant indices) and part of 1.3; Layer 3 has 3.1 to 3.6 and 3.8; Layer 7 has 7.2 and 7.3. Mathlib supplies the substrate throughout: IsArithFrobAt, KummerDedekind, differentIdeal with transitivity, Ideal.relNorm, IsDecompositionField/IsInertiaField, sign_discr, the regulator API, and Dirichlet's unit theorem. What is genuinely missing is the completion dictionary and everything downstream of it. Layer 5 has only 5.1 (which is fully built, with the residue field and its cardinality) and 5.2 (completionAlgHom with continuity, its continuous universal property and tower composition); 5.3 to 5.10 - the semilocal equivalence, norm and trace over the places above v, the invariant matching, decompositionHom, the completed integer rings, the localization of the different and the discriminant valuation - do not exist. Layer 6 is entirely absent and cannot be stated, because its supplier (the local lower ramification filtration) does not exist either; the only ramification filtration in the baseline is TauCeti's for places of a function field. Also missing: 1.5 (totally split in the Galois closure and in composita), 3.7 (Dedekind's criterion), 3.9 and 3.10 (Dedekind's theorem on cycle types, though the fullCycleType bookkeeping it needs is built), 3.11 (common index divisors), 7.1 (the subfield dictionary), 7.4 (explicit unit certification, so no exact regulator at positive rank), and Layer 8's label predicate and worked suite.
